title: Runtime mux policy introspection — workbench jot
content:
Goal / motivation:
- Quick scratchpad for a lightweight introspection API and a dev workbench to debug runtime muxing decisions.
- Problem: policies (weights, fallbacks, region preferences, tenant overrides) are opaque during deployment. When a request takes a suboptimal path we need a deterministic way to reproduce and inspect the decision tree.

Non-goals:
- Not trying to replace the policy engine or rollout DSL. This is for engineering/debugging only (and limited telemetry).

High-level approach (sketch):
1) Add a read-only /introspect endpoint that returns the computed decision graph for a single request.
2) Provide an evaluate endpoint that accepts a synthetic request blob and returns the chosen route plus the intermediate scoring breakdowns.
3) Build a tiny local dev workbench (CLI + minimal UI) that can hit evaluate and render human-readable traces.

API shapes (draft):
- POST /v1/policies/evaluate
  payload: {"request": {..inbound metadata..}, "policy_id": "x", "trace_level": "detailed"}
  response: {
    "route": "hosted:tok-12a",
    "variant": "gptq-6b-q4b",
    "score_breakdown": [
      {"step": "tenant_override", "score": 35, "reason": "tenant T has explicit routing to dedicated"},
      {"step": "region_pref", "score": 10, "reason": "eu-preferred, but eu saturated => penalty"},
      {"step": "cost_bucket", "score": -5, "reason": "dedicated cost saving"}
    ],
    "final_score": 40,
    "evaluated_at": "2024-09-10T18:22:03Z"
  }

- GET /v1/policies/introspect?request_id=abc123
  response: {
    "request_id": "abc123",
    "resolved_policy_version": "policy-2024-09-08-3",
    "decision_graph": "(text-graph representation, see below)",
    "trace_link": "(optional link to longer trace blob)"
  }

Decision graph text format (very small):
- Represent graph as newline indented nodes. Example:
  root
    tenant-override -> dedicated-pool-A (score 35)
    else -> region-check
      eu -> hosted-eu (score 12)
      us -> hosted-us (score 8)

  Rationale: keeps the payload small and easy to paste into bug reports. We can extend to dotgraph later.

Telemetry and privacy constraints:
- Introspection API is restricted to internal tooling only (authz). Must not leak PII or prompt contents.
- Default redact level: prompt -> truncated to 128 chars and token counts, attachments removed.
- Add explicit flag "allow_prompt_dump" for SRE with extra audit logging (must be recorded).

Integration with existing runtime components (notes):
- Policy evaluation happens in the router stage. We will add a deterministic RNG seed derived from request_id so evaluate(eid) == production evaluation for same inputs/version.
- Need to persist policy_version id with request traces (already done for 60% of requests; fill gaps).
- Evaluate endpoint should be side-effect free (no allocations of temp capacity or reservations). If policy normally triggers a reservation, evaluate returns "would_reserve": {"pool": "ded-A", "expected_latency": 45} rather than actually reserving.

Workbench: CLI features to build first iteration:
- local-eval --policy policy-2024-09-08-3 --payload sample.json --format text|json
- expand-trace --request-id abc123 --pretty
- quick-hypothesize: compare two policy versions for same input and show diff in route+scores

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: How to handle multi-hop fallbacks where runtime tries hosted->dedicated->private in series? Do we show entire timeline or only final chosen path?
  - Proposal: show full timeline with timestamps and per-hop metrics (attempted/resolved).
- Q: What scope of metadata must be included to reproduce decision (tenant id, feature flags, recent-telemetry snapshot)?
  - Minimal reproducible set: tenant_id, request_type, region_hint, model_family, selected_tier. If reproduction fails, CLI should surface missing contexts.
- Q: Rate limiting for evaluate endpoint (avoid noisy internal scripts generating heavy load).
  - Put guard rails: per-user per-minute quotas, and require a dev token with elevated quota.

Edge cases to consider:
- Stale policy versions: if request used old policy but current live policy differs, introspect must show both the live and the resolved policy used by the request.
- Non-deterministic scoring components (e.g., probabilistic trial bucketing). Use explicit seed and record it.
- Tenant overrides via config-store reloads mid-request: record config revision at eval-time.

Developer checklist (minimal MVP):
- [ ] Spec API contract and JSON schema (this doc)
- [ ] Implement evaluate endpoint (router-level hook) returning score_breakdown + mock reservation info
- [ ] Add request_id-to-policy_version logging in router (if missing)
- [ ] Build CLI with two commands (local-eval, expand-trace)
- [ ] Add authz policies for introspection (internal-only)
- [ ] Add redaction rules and tests

Quick implementation notes:
- Keep evaluate as a separate micro-handler that imports the router policy evaluation function but runs in-process. That avoids changing the hot path.
- Cache compiled policy graphs per version in memory to speed repeated evaluate calls. TTL ~ 5m.
- Use same scoring function entrypoints; pass deterministic seed via header X-Eval-Seed to make sampling deterministic.

Example minimal payload for local-eval (paste into CLI):
{
  "request": {
    "tenant_id": "tenant-xyz",
    "request_type": "text-generation",
    "model_family": "gptx-6b",
    "region_hint": "eu",
    "token_budget": 512
  },
  "policy_id": "global-mux-v2",
  "trace_level": "detailed"
}

Notes / stream-of-consciousness:
- Good to have a 'why' field in score_breakdown entries (helps triage).
- We'll likely iterate on the small text graph format. Want something that copies/pastes into Slack without being huge.
- Consider an option to 'simulate_load' that replays a micro-batch of requests and shows batch-aware routing (batch transparency matters).
- Keep the first pass internal only. If product wants a surfaced customer-facing explanation later, we can shrink and sanitize output.

References & related work:
- related: runtime-routing-rule-compiler-spec-draft (confluence)
- related: ingress-telemetry-privacy-masking-playbook (notes on redaction)
- related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform PR#8342 (policy eval refactor)

Next steps (this week):
- Pair with Samir on a quick PoC for evaluate (in dev cluster) and wire CLI to hit it.
- Get sign-off from platform lead (Priya) on redaction defaults.

Recorded quick decisions (will move to ADR later):
- Introspection API internal-only and auth gated — accepted 2024-09-12 by Priya.
- Evaluate endpoint side-effect free and returns "would_reserve" — accepted 2024-09-14 by Samir.

-- end of jot --
